note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, hour, price and lighting answer below comes from the City of Irvine's own pages: its pickleball page, its court regulations page, and each park's own page. Irvine states every published count twice, once in a sentence and once in an amenity list, and the three venues where the two records agree are published. Where the City is silent, on parking and on surface, this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking:
The City of Irvine publishes nothing about parking at any of these three parks. The word appears on none of its pickleball, court regulations or park pages.

What each park page carries instead is an acreage and an amenity list, and those say what kind of site you are arriving at. Mike Ward Community Park is approximately 22 acres, with lighted basketball and racquetball courts, a sand volleyball court and three restrooms. Portola Springs Community Park is approximately 32 acres, with a community centre, lighted softball fields, soccer fields and tennis courts, and two restrooms. Heritage Community Park is the largest at approximately 36.5 acres, with twelve lighted tennis courts, a lake, a splash pad and four restrooms. Restrooms are stated at all three parks. A lot, a fee or a permit is not.
slots.peak_hours:
Irvine states no peak times. It states instead a set of rules for how a court is shared. All three parks are open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily, and every one of the eighteen courts is lit, so the window is sixteen hours long and does not shrink at dusk. The court regulations say: "Open courts are on a first-come, first-serve basis. Please use the waiting board where available." When others are waiting, doubles is limited to 60 minutes and singles to 30, warm-up included. If nobody is waiting you may carry on.

Four courts run on a different clock. Courts #3 and #4 at Mike Ward and Courts #5 and #6 at Portola Springs can be reserved online "between the hours of 7 a.m. to noon, and 4 to 10 p.m.", in one- or two-hour blocks. Residents may book five days ahead and non-residents three. When nobody has booked them these courts revert to drop-in play. City sponsored programmes have priority over all other use.
slots.surface_condition:
The City names no surface for any pickleball court in Irvine. No park page says what the courts are made of, and neither the regulations page nor the pickleball page does. What the City does write, consistently, is the word lit. Each count appears twice, as "eight lit pickleball courts" on the pickleball page and "8 Lighted Pickleball Courts" in the park's amenity list, and the same pairing holds for the six at Portola Springs and the four at Heritage.

All eighteen are counted as pickleball courts. The City lists hybrid tennis and pickleball courts at other parks, including Heritage, but gives only a city-wide total for them, so none is added to any venue here. On a tennis court the regulations are explicit: "Tennis courts are designated solely for tennis use", and if tennis players arrive "those playing pickleball or badminton must vacate the court". Tennis shoes are required on every City court.
slots.local_scene:
Eighteen verified courts across three parks, every one lit in the City's own word, every park open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Irvine is the first California city on this site. Courts #3 and #4 at Mike Ward Community Park and Courts #5 and #6 at Portola Springs Community Park can be booked at "Resident Rate: $17/hr" and "Non-Resident Rate: $19/hr". The other fourteen courts are first come, first served and the City states no price for them.

The City runs junior, adult and private lessons at all three parks through contract instructors, and a league, Irvine Team Pickleball, at Portola Springs: eight teams, a seven-week round robin and three-week playoffs, self-rated at 3.5, $490 per team per season. The City also says it "is evaluating building pickleball courts at the Great Park".

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts under lights
best_for.text: Mike Ward Community Park has eight lit pickleball courts, the largest set in Irvine, open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily in a 22-acre park with three restrooms, lighted basketball and racquetball courts and a sand volleyball court. Six courts are first come, first served; Courts #3 and #4 can be booked online at $17 an hour for residents and $19 for non-residents.

best_for.heading: Best if you want organised play
best_for.text: Portola Springs Community Park has six lit courts and is the home of Irvine Team Pickleball, the City's league: eight teams, a seven-week round robin, three weeks of playoffs, self-rated 3.5, $490 per team per season. Courts #5 and #6 are reservable at the same $17 and $19 rates as Mike Ward, and the City's contract instructors teach lessons here. Open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to turn up and play
best_for.text: Heritage Community Park has four lit courts and no reservation system: every court is first come, first served under the City's regulations, with a waiting board and a 60-minute doubles limit when others are waiting. It is the largest park of the three at 36.5 acres, with twelve lighted tennis courts, a lake, a splash pad and four restrooms, open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Irvine have?
faqs.a: Eighteen are verified across three City parks: eight at Mike Ward Community Park, six at Portola Springs Community Park and four at Heritage Community Park, each count stated twice by the City. The City itself publishes more than one total. Its regulations page says "12 public pickleball courts", while its own per-park sentence on the pickleball page adds to twenty.

faqs.q: Why is Los Olivos Community Park not listed?
faqs.a: Because the City states two different counts for it. The pickleball page and the court regulations page both say "two lit pickleball courts"; the park's own amenity list says "3 Lighted Pickleball Courts". The rule here is to publish the number the operator states, and that rule cannot choose between two numbers. The address, 101 Alfonso, resolves and the courts are lit; it fails on the count alone.

sources.evidence: The City's pickleball page. "The City of Irvine has eight lit pickleball courts located at Mike Ward Community Park, six lit pickleball courts located at Portola Springs Community Park, four lit pickleball courts located at Heritage Park, and two lit pickleball courts located at Los Olivos Community Park. In addition, there are 10 hybrid tennis and pickleball courts located at the following parks: Heritage, Knollcrest, Los Olivos, Portola Springs, San Carlo, Turtle Rock, and University." "Pickleball court reservations are now available at Portola Springs Community Park (Courts #5 and #6) and Mike Ward Community Park (Courts #3 and #4). Residents may book up to five days in advance, while non-residents may book three days in advance." "Resident Rate: $17/hr", "Non-Resident Rate: $19/hr". "Reservations can be made in one or two hour increments, with individuals allowed to have one reservation per day." "Courts can be reserved Monday through Sunday, between the hours of 7 a.m. to noon, and 4 to 10 p.m." The reservable courts "can be used for drop-in play if there is no reservation or if a reservation no-shows"; "Please immediately vacate the court if a reservation holder arrives during their allotted time." Lessons "at Mike Ward Community Park, Portola Springs Community Park and Heritage Park". Irvine Team Pickleball at "Portola Springs Community Park - Pickleball Courts", "Address: 900 Tomato Springs, Irvine, CA 92618": "Eight teams face off in a 7-week Round Robin and a 3-week single-elimination playoffs", "a self-rated level 3.5 league", "Cost is $490 per team per season". "the City is evaluating building pickleball courts at the Great Park." Snapshot: data/sources/irvine/pickleball.html

Heritage, Knollcrest, Los Olivos, San Carlo, Turtle Rock and University Community Park "have hybrid courts where players may choose to play tennis or pickleball. Tennis shoes are required."
